newsitem.title: USA: W. House hopes for Senate approval of Fed nominees.
newsitem.headline: W. House hopes for Senate approval of Fed nominees.

text.p: A senior White House official voiced hopes on Thursday that President Clinton's nominees to the Federal Reserve board would win Senate confirmation.
"All the feedback I've gotten was positive," said Gene Sperling, head of Clinton's National Economic Council. "We're hopeful they will be reviewed and confirmed in due course."

Clinton announced earlier he would nominate University of Michigan professor Edward Gramlich and economic consultant Roger Ferguson to the Fed board. Speaking to reporters, Sperling described the two men as "sound and pragmatic."
Gramlich will succeed Janet Yellen, who left the Fed earlier this year to become White House chief economist. That term expires on Jan. 31, 2008.

Ferguson will take up the position vacated by Lawrence Lindsey, who left the central bank in February to join the American Enterprise Institute, a conservative think tank here. That term expires on Jan. 31, 2000.
